kill_fact: The terminal-erosion moat gate fails on primary sources: there is no evidence of durable pricing power or rising returns — the filings show the OPPOSITE, and the one hard catalyst was rejected by the market inside two sessions. Pricing power: Q1 2026 domestic broadband ARPU fell ~3.1% (the 10-Q attributes the broadband revenue decline to 'lower average rates'; no annual rate increase, migration to simplified national pricing, free wireless lines), with management guiding MORE ARPU pressure through Q2 2026 — an explicitly price-concessive defense, the opposite of a moat. Returns: ROIC ~6.3-6.8% TTM is below any reasonable cost of capital and falling (Q1 2026 net income -35.6% to $2.17B, diluted EPS $0.60 vs $0.89 = -33%), and the cash-cow Connectivity & Platforms segment's Adjusted EBITDA decline is ACCELERATING (-4.3% YoY in Q1 2026, $7.910B vs $8.264B, vs -3.7% in Q3 2025), exactly on management's guided-worse path. Capital returns are no longer even rising: buybacks are PAUSED for the ~12-month separation (Cavanagh, June 29 investor call), removing the per-share support the deterministic screen counted as 'returns rising'. And the breakup catalyst both FIRED and was REFUSED: the June 29, 2026 announcement popped ~22% pre-market (~$28) but closed only ~+4.5% that day and traded ~$23.6-$25.0 by July 1 — essentially back at the pre-announcement ~$23.17. The market looked at the sum-of-the-parts unlock for two full sessions and declined to pay it, leaving a ~12-month soft execution path (Form 10, unresolved allocation of ~$85B net debt) in which the CMCSA holder keeps the melting cable RemainCo while the rising-return assets (theme parks >$1B quarterly EBITDA, studios, Peacock) leave with the NBCUniversal SpinCo.
corrections: STALE ANCHOR in the bear's own risk_reward: it is computed 'from the post-announcement ~$28 price', but ~$28 was only the June 29 pre-market print. The stock closed roughly +4.5% on June 29 and traded ~$23.6-$25.0 on July 1, 2026 — the announcement premium is gone. Cuts both ways: entry is ~15% cheaper than the debate modeled (mechanically better asymmetry to the ~$50 SoP base), but the fade is itself evidence the market rejects the SoP re-rate; the 'momentum buyers piled in' washout framing is moot.

NUMBER TRUTH — FCF overstated and turning down: Comcast's own reported FCF was $19.2B for FY2025 (record) and $3.901B in Q1 2026 vs $5.421B in Q1 2025 (-28% YoY), giving ~$17.7B TTM on the company's definition — not the $20.4B in the thesis (~13-15% overstated; the higher figure is a data-vendor FCF variant). Cheapness is still real (~5x P/FCF at ~$24.5 on ~$17.7B), but the '3.8x / 20%+ yield' framing is stale and the trajectory is negative.

CAPITAL RETURNS CORRECTION: the 'roughly 65% of free cash flow paid out each quarter' run-rate no longer holds — share repurchases are paused for the ~one-year separation process (June 29, 2026 investor call); the $0.33/quarter dividend is stated to stay intact. Both entities are targeted at investment-grade balance sheets, but the $94.6B-total-debt allocation between them is not yet public.

STALE ANCHOR in the SoP Media line: the $27.1B Media revenue base predates the Versant separation (completed January 2, 2026; Q1 2026 results exclude Versant with pro-forma restatement). Post-Versant Media revenue was $7.28B in Q1 2026 — and that quarter was inflated by the Milan Olympics + Super Bowl ('+60.8% YoY'). The post-spin Media run-rate is materially below $27.1B, so both bull and bear SoP overstate Media EV on today's asset base.

Share count: SoP uses ~3.78B shares; Q1 2026 10-Q diluted weighted-average is 3,617M (down from 3,784M a year earlier) — per-share SoP values are understated ~4-5% (works in the thesis's favor; does not offset the moat failure).

Numbers that DO verify: net debt ~$85B ($94.6B total debt less ~$9.5B cash, Q1 2026 10-Q); latest-quarter EPS -33% YoY; broadband net losses -65K (improved 117K YoY, though over half the improvement was attributed to one-off 'Legendary February' promotions); record wireless adds 435K; the June 29, 2026 tax-free spin announcement (NBCUniversal+Sky+parks media company vs cable/broadband/wireless Comcast, Cavanagh/Angelakis CEOs, ~mid-2027 target) is real per the Form 8-K.
evidence: Comcast Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1, 2026-06-29 (SEC EDGAR accession 0000950103-26-009591): announcement of separation into two public companies via tax-free spin-off of NBCUniversal incl. Sky, expected to complete in ~one year; Mike Cavanagh CEO of NBCUniversal, Michael Angelakis CEO of Comcast post-separation; buybacks paused during separation per the same-day investor call, dividend intact.

Comcast Form 10-Q, quarter ended 2026-03-31 (SEC EDGAR, cmcsa-20260331.htm): net income -35.6% to $2.174B, diluted EPS $0.60 vs $0.89 (-33% YoY); total debt reduced to $94.6B post-Versant (cash ~$9.5B → ~$85B net debt); domestic broadband revenue down on 'lower average rates'; diluted weighted-average shares 3,617M.

Comcast Q1 2026 earnings release, 2026-04-23 (Business Wire / Comcast IR): free cash flow $3.901B vs $5.421B in Q1 2025 (-28% YoY); Connectivity & Platforms Adjusted EBITDA $7.910B, -4.3% YoY (accelerating from -3.7% in Q3 2025); broadband net losses 65K (improved 117K YoY); record 435K wireless line adds; Media segment revenue $7.280B with Versant excluded (separation completed 2026-01-02, pro-forma restated); broadband ARPU ~-3.1% with further pressure guided through Q2 2026 per the earnings call.

Comcast Q4 2025 results, 2026-01 (cmcsa.com IR): FY2025 free cash flow $19.2B (record) — with Q1 2026 down $1.5B YoY, TTM FCF on Comcast's own definition is ~$17.7B, not the $20.4B used in the thesis. Market reaction to the spin: June 29, 2026 close ~+4.5% (Fortune/Yahoo Finance market coverage, 2026-06-29), trading ~$23.6-$25.0 on 2026-07-01 vs ~$23.17 pre-announcement — the ~22% pre-market pop fully faded.
